transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I’ve been planning my days around avoiding driving over high bridges. If I can take another route, I do, even if it’s out of the way. And if I can’t avoid it, I just grip the wheel and get through it, but it’s pretty rough.
How long have you been avoiding driving over high bridges, and does the fear feel excessive or out of proportion to the actual danger?

I think it is out of proportion, yeah. I mean, I know those bridges over the bay are built fine and people drive over them every day without anything happening. But when I get close to one, my mind just goes straight to, like, the car could go right over the side.
Does this fear of driving over high bridges cause you a lot of stress or interfere with your daily life, such as work, errands, or seeing friends?

Yeah, it does some. I still get to work and I still see people, so it hasn’t stopped my life, but I do work around it. I leave earlier because I take longer routes to avoid certain bridges. And I’ve turned down some fishing trips because I didn’t want to deal with the drive. It makes me feel like I’m not as independent as I used to be.
Do you feel anxious or on edge in the hours or minutes before you have to drive over a high bridge?
Yeah, mostly once I can see it coming up. My chest gets tight, my hands start sweating on the wheel, and I just kind of stare straight ahead like, okay, just get to the other side.
Do you ever feel similar anxiety or avoid other situations, like being in crowds, open spaces, or specific places?
No, not really. I haven’t noticed it in crowds or open spaces or places like that. It seems pretty tied to those high bridges when I’m driving.
Have you ever felt similar anxiety or avoided other specific situations, such as being in enclosed spaces, flying, or being in social situations where you might be judged?
Not that I can think of. I don’t like being uncomfortable, sure, but I don’t avoid elevators or flying or social stuff because of anxiety. It’s really just the driving over those high bridges.
